findings.claim: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Netflix reported revenue of $12,874,176 thousand, up 12% from $11,510,307 thousand, operating income of $4,458,600 thousand, up 37%, an operating margin of 34.6% versus 28.2%, net income of $3,663,927 thousand, up 44%, and diluted EPS of $0.87 versus $0.59.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Third-quarter revenue growth came from a $1,057 million increase in subscription revenue, reflecting higher memberships and pricing, and a $256 million increase in advertising revenue; for the nine months, subscription revenue rose $3,472 million and advertising revenue rose $864 million.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The October 20, 2026 shareholder letter forecasts fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of $13,442 million, operating income of $3,500 million, an operating margin of 26.0% and diluted EPS of $0.67, and full-year 2026 revenue of $51.1 billion, up 13%, with an operating margin of 31.5% versus 29.5% in 2025 and operating-income growth of more than 20%.

Netflix cut its 2026 advertising-revenue expectation to about $2.7 billion from about $3 billion because some ad-product capabilities rolled out more slowly than expected, putting full-year revenue 0.2% below the midpoint of the prior forecast range, and cut 2026 free-cash-flow guidance to about $12.0 billion from $12.5 billion, primarily because of a real-estate transaction expected to close in the fourth quarter.

In the third quarter of 2026 Netflix repurchased 63,917,979 shares for $4.8 billion, and for the nine months it repurchased 130,349,765 shares for $10.7 billion, leaving $22.3 billion of repurchase authorization; the April 2026 board authorization added $25 billion.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On February 27, 2026, Warner Bros. Discovery terminated the amended merger agreement under which Netflix would have acquired WBD's streaming and studios businesses, and Paramount Skydance paid Netflix a $2.8 billion termination fee that was recorded in interest and other income in the first quarter of 2026; related acquisition financing was terminated with nothing borrowed.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: At September 30, 2026, Netflix had $15,132 million of notes outstanding, of which $2,475 million net of issuance costs was classified as short-term debt, long-term debt on the balance sheet was $12,657,598 thousand versus $13,463,971 thousand at December 31, 2025, cash and cash equivalents were $8,194,275 thousand, and debt-issuance proceeds in the quarter were $992,550 thousand.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Streaming content obligations were $25,222,800 thousand at September 30, 2026, up from $24,039,228 thousand at December 31, 2025, and additions to content assets in the third quarter were $5,159,790 thousand versus $4,653,935 thousand a year earlier.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Year-over-year revenue growth slowed to 11.8% in the third quarter of 2026 from 17.2% in the third quarter of 2025, and the company said there is investor concern about view-hours growth even though 2026 price-change retention was consistent with prior changes and global and U.S. churn improved year over year.

Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow included $729 million of non-routine payments for Brazilian non-income tax assessments covering prior periods, and the year-ago third quarter included a $619 million expense for Brazilian non-income tax assessments that did not repeat.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The fourth-quarter 2026 operating-margin forecast of 26.0% includes about 120 basis points of cost from recently announced headcount reductions, and the full-year 31.5% margin guide includes about 30 basis points from those reductions.

Netflix said its audience is approaching one billion people, that it secured a new Disney licensing deal covering current and library series and films, and that it will introduce the advertising tier in 15 new countries in 2027, with the first launches in March 2027 covering nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru and New Zealand.

The shareholder letter reports third-quarter free cash flow, defined as operating cash flow minus purchases of property and equipment, of $2,883,513 thousand versus $2,660,455 thousand a year earlier, and nine-month free cash flow of $9,502,756 thousand versus $7,588,746 thousand.

Currencies other than the U.S. dollar accounted for 57% of revenue and 30% of operating expenses in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and third-quarter stock-based compensation was $134 million versus $81 million a year earlier.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On November 14, 2025 Netflix completed a ten-for-one forward stock split, with the record date of November 10, 2025; per-share figures in the 2026 10-Q are retroactively adjusted, and the split was not a capital raise. Diluted weighted-average shares fell to 4,195,127 thousand in the third quarter of 2026 from 4,340,392 thousand a year earlier.
findings.source_title: Netflix, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

upcoming_catalysts.event: Fourth-quarter 2026 results against the company forecast of $13,442 million of revenue, $3,500 million of operating income, a 26.0% operating margin and diluted EPS of $0.67.
First tranche of advertising-tier launches in March 2027 in nine EMEA countries, Colombia, Peru and New Zealand, part of a 15-country expansion.
Approximately $1 billion debt maturity in the fourth quarter of 2026, which the company said the quarter's bond issuance was intended to fund.

policy_links.policy: Inflation Reduction Act 1% excise tax on stock repurchases
policy_links.bottleneck: cash cost of returning capital through buybacks
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The tax does not create revenue. The 10-Q states that the $4.8 billion third-quarter and $10.7 billion nine-month repurchase totals exclude the 1% excise tax.

key_risks.risk: 2026 advertising revenue is now expected at about $2.7 billion, about $300 million below the prior approximately $3 billion outlook, because ad-product capabilities are rolling out more slowly than planned.
Streaming content obligations were $25.2 billion at September 30, 2026, and quarterly additions to content assets rose to $5.16 billion from $4.65 billion.
Revenue growth decelerated to 11.8% from 17.2% a year earlier, and management acknowledged investor concern about view-hours growth.
Brazilian non-income tax assessments produced a $619 million expense in the year-ago quarter and $729 million of cash payments in the first nine months of 2026.
Fifty-seven percent of nine-month revenue was denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar.

notes: No equity offering, ATM or convertible issuance was found in the Q3 2026 10-Q. The November 14, 2025 ten-for-one split did not raise capital and share counts in the filing are split-adjusted. The shareholder-letter prose says fourth-quarter revenue growth of 12%, while the forecast table shows $13,442 million and 11.5% growth; the table figures are used here. Membership totals are not disclosed. The third-quarter margin beat was attributed to expense timing. The $2.8 billion WBD termination fee inflates nine-month net income and operating cash flow. The letter's approximate $1 billion bond and maturity figures are consistent with the 10-Q proceeds from issuance of debt of $992,550 thousand. No going-concern language was found.
